subject: Inference deployment procurement pathways — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-27T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Inference deployment procurement pathways — recap & next steps

Hi Sara / Ben,

Thanks again for the time this morning — good discussion framing Lumina's two primary workloads (clinical summarization at ~6k tokens/session, and high-volume embeddings for search/triage). Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Peak concurrency: ~120 simultaneous summarization sessions across regionally distributed clinics.
- Typical session: 3–8k tokens; 95th latency target ~600ms.
- Embeddings: bulk ingestion daily (~10M vectors) with moderate realtime query QPS.
- Data controls: HIPAA-adjacent; prefer VPC or dedicated isolation; audit logs are a must.

Deployment paths we discussed (high level)
1) Hosted API (fastest): Per-token billing, streaming, simple integration. Pros: no infra ops, immediate SLAs. Cons: unit economics not optimal for sustained, high token volumes.
2) Dedicated Reserved (reserved GPU pools): Monthly commit, predictable throughput, lower $/token at scale. Pros: cost predictability and isolation; can hit latency targets. Cons: monthly commit required; provisioning lead time.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer-managed runtime, strongest data isolation and KMS/HSM integration. Pros: full control, compliance alignment. Cons: higher upfront setup and fixed costs (CAPEX/OPEX).

Attached a first-pass cost model with 3 scenarios (per-token hosted, 6/12-month reserved commit ranges, and a rough private deployment opex+one-time setup). See "Lumina_cost_model_v2.xlsx". Key ask: please confirm which procurement committees need the price breakouts (IT procurement vs Finance vs Security).

Next steps proposed
- You: confirm primary procurement owner + any internal cutover dates (we heard Q4 for pilot).
- Redwood: Priyom to produce an optimized reserved-commit sizing and RFP-ready summary; I will produce a one‑page cost comparison for your finance team.
- Follow-up meeting: propose Thu 05/29 10:00am PT (30m) — Priyom and Rishi to join for technical and commercial questions.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sara / Marissa — quick technical summary and what I'll bring to the follow-up call: 

Technical assumptions I used for the cost model (detailed in the attached workbook):
- Summarization workload: average 4.5k tokens/output, peak 120 concurrent sessions, 95th token latency target 600ms.
- Embeddings ingestion: 10M vectors/day; indexing and query load assumed 200 QPS during business hours.
- Model: LlamaX-70B (quantized) for summarization; a small embedding model for vector generation.

Preliminary economics (high-level numbers from the workbook)
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): ~$0.00006 per token, estimated monthly spend at pilot scale = ~$85k (month 1 with validation overhead).
- Dedicated Reserved (medium commit: 4x A100-class GPUs reserved): effective $/token falls ~40% vs hosted at steady state; monthly commit estimate = $42k–$55k depending on utilization assumptions.
- Private VPC/On-prem: one-time setup and integration ~ $120k (professional services + deployment); monthly infra + ops ~= $35k–$50k depending on redundancy. Break-even horizon vs hosted: ~3–6 months depending on utilization and piloting ramp.

Security artifacts I'll bring: SOC2 summary page, network architecture template for VPC deployment, audit log export sample.

I'll prepare a one‑slide RFP-ready summary of commit sizing (3 commit tiers) and the trade-offs. Will attach that to the calendar invite.

Cheers,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
